title: Abby Holliday, Charli Adams
description: Abby Holliday + Charli Adams There comes a time in every artist’s career when the art form transcends a mere outlet for self-expression and becomes a universal gift to mankind. For some it takes years, for Abby Holliday it was there from the start. Her vulnerable introspection and brutal lyricism combined with mind-bending sonic sensibilities and a distinct production style immediately fused a bond between her and her loyal fan base. Holliday masterfully guides listeners through moments in time extremely specific to her own life that puts words to collective experiences of the human condition, reaching into places we might not have known existed prior. Abby found her voice during her early years of college where she began quietly writing songs in the confines of her room. After a friend heard the songs and encouraged her to share them, Abby met producer Jonathan Class and set off to record her debut album WHEN WE’RE FAR APART I FALL APART. It was in these studio moments where Abby’s sound began to take shape, a launchpad for her sophomore album I’M OK NO I’M NOT. Holliday and Class experiment with a wide range of sounds from vocoded vocal stacks, to jarring synths, to lush strings and piano, to a tasteful blend of organic and synthetic rhythm sections amassing in a discography that runs the gambit of the most beautiful songs to songs that smack you in the face with unforgettable hooks and driving beats. CRACK A SMILE COME ON STAY A WHILE, Holliday’s highly anticipated junior record, is out now. “Former cheer captain” isn’t something you always see on the resume of a rising, alternative singer-songwriter. For Charli Adams, who grew up across several small towns in rural Alabama, an outward display of optimism might have been the only way to get by. title: Lucky Gold Jr. & Werewolf
description: Lucky Gold Jr. & Werewolf SHOW DESCRIPTION: Two East-Coast-via-Ohio based indie projects will be rocking the Rockwell on August 11th with support from a secret special guest! ARTIST BIOS: Lucky Gold Jr. is a folk-rock project led by Massachusetts-based singer-songwriter Ellie Fallon, with frequent live and recorded support from her sibling Mimi Fallon on bass, and producer, instrumentalist, & friend Ollie Peterson. Fallon has anchored her sound to nostalgia’s ephemera, unraveling unique experiences with familiar language. She writes about everything from failure to fandom with a perspective informed by hope, and a sound inspired by her collaborators and musical fixations alike. Oliver Peterson, under the name Werewolf, records alone from his carpet-padded garage in Stamford, Connecticut. Through one-wire systems, meticulously-crafted ambient textures, and natural melodic sensibilities, Peterson produces a sophisticated sound that ascends the parts of its sum, and escapes time and place while kneeling in worship to it. Werewolf marries the grounded – acoustic guitars, crunchy drums, raw vocals – with the ethereal – swirling drones, surreally visceral lyricism, abstract visual components – to build a dream pop, shoegaze, indie-rock vision that is entirely his own. title: The Darkness Behind
description: The Darkness Behind SHOW DESCRIPTION: The Darkness Behind is a solo multimedia performance that explores the many meanings behind the title: surviving darkness, leaving darkness behind, and the ongoing tension between memory and freedom. Ameen’s musical journey during the ISIS occupation of his hometown in Iraq, Mosul, 2014-2017, and the musical chapters post that period. Using violin, voice, live looping, and electronic textures, the performance combines cinematic music, experimental sound, and personal storytelling that creates an immersive live experience. This work follows performances at venues including The Metropolitan Museum of Art and One World Trade Center. ARTIST BIO: Award-winning Iraqi composer, performer, and multidisciplinary artist, born In Baghdad 1989. title: Kooked Out, Viper Cut Eyes, Stunt
description: Kooked Out, Viper Cut Eyes, Stunt SHOW DESCRIPTION: The Scene Within the Scene is a local community building platform for artists and musicians to connect and support one another. This is the first show curated by this group which is completely non profit. The bands on this first show are High Energy Rock bands with influences from Garage/Surf Punk/ and Psych Rock. ARTIST BIOS: Kooked Out: “The kaleidoscopic sound of Kooked Out has evolved naturally throughout the years and draws influences from almost every genre and decade of music from the 1930s to present day, crafting a unique mix of styles and sounds that have developed Kooked Out a cult-like following in the skate and surf communities. Leaning heavily into the music of the ’50s, ’60s and early 2000s, Kooked Out’s genre-spanning sound has become a calling card, both on record and live on stage, appropriate for a creative outlet that lists its top influences as The White Stripes, The Beatles, Jimi Hendrix, Dick Dale, The Black Keys, Cage The Elephant, and Blink-182.” -Michael Marotta / Knyvet Members: John Fiore, Chris Laskey, Chris Caduto, Emily Trubey / ‘2024 Live Act Of The Year’ New England Music Awards Viper Cut Eyes: Boston’s unapologetically noisy and transcendent Surfadelic Psych Rock unit Ace McGuire’s Acid Tabs are defibrillating stagnant bodies with blood pulsing riffs paired with a hit of tape echoed and verbed out psychedelia. Originally a bedroom recording project of Bermudian singer and songwriter Liv Dunks and New Bedford MA’s guitarist, singer and producer Mitch Cardoza, they expanded their vision by adding San Francisco’s multi-instrumentalist Erik Dietz on bass. Stunt!: Brings the attitude and aggression of 90s Rock bands to today’s pop music scene. Riffs inspired by the grunge and pop-punk sounds of yesterday meld with vocal melodies that hang with any of today’s radio ear worms. Social Medias: @thescenewithinthescene / @kookedoutofficial / @viper.cut.eyes / @thebandstunt DOORS: 7:00 PM SHOW

title: EVERFINER Shimmer Funk Cosmic Gala
description: EVERFINER Shimmer Funk Cosmic Gala SHOW DESCRIPTION: Join EVERFINER in a cosmic shimmer celebration of music as the group conjures its 2nd EP, Shimmer Funk, from the depths of Nova 37 in EFNR Star Belt. You may find yourself unable to stop dancing to these tunes, but fear not. Shimmer Funk has been crafted over the past year with the magical properties required to get your body moving and grooving. Resume your position on the bridge, strap into the cockpit of your star vessel, and prepare for a shimmer space journey. ARTIST BIOS: EVERFINER is a Boston based six-piece ensemble rocking thoughtful originals in overlapping genres including, shimmer-folk, shimmer-funk, soul, and pop. BIG HUGE harmonies lay on top of a tight, minimalist rhythm section, and if you’re lucky a horn section will casually be lowered from the rafters. Lyrically, these tunes work through issues of identity, boundaries, long distance relationships, short distance situationships, and the flux of family. The band is a beautiful collective of musicians who care as much about each other as they do about their art. As we all grow and learn, each day we are all becoming a little more EVERFINER. title: Nelward
description: Nelward nelward is an innovative music artist creating funky electronic artpop for the internet age. Early on, the melodies of classic Nintendo games were etched into his ADHD brain and never seemed to leave. Drawing from a wide array of influences, nelward enjoys the explorative aspect of music creation and is not one to dwell in one sound for too long. He is also known for the colorful and whimsical art direction in his often self-produced videos. In 2017, his first EP Alive in Screen established his foundational sound. The subsequent success of the new jack swing/nu metal banger Ghost / Getting Better and bubblegum pop earworm Never Wanna Fall in Love With U established him as a force to be reckoned with in the independent electronic music scene. 2020’s Eat Your Dreams EP delved into heavier subject matter while tightening nelward’s knack for catchy songwriting. 2024’s single THE RUNAROUND combines infectious earworms while embracing musical exploration. Nelward is known for his animated live performances, completing a 40+ date tour of North America and Europe with TWRP from 2024-2025. In 2025 the nelward live band was born, representing a distinct chapter in the evolution of his live performance. Nelward represents a growing segment of independent electronic artists who are building significant followings through digital platforms while creating innovative multimedia art experiences. Justice Cow is the cosmic gumbo of Jessica Kion. She grew up in a musical family which meant pressing rewind until she had transcribed every word of the “Grease” soundtrack and being forced to sing barbershop quartet family-style in the car. For over a decade she has toured extensively across the US and abroad, equally at home in living rooms, rock clubs, and festival stages. title: Mr. Phylzzz and friends
description: Mr. Phylzzz and friends Chicago spreads their net of sonic oddities throughout our great nation as two piece noise rockers Mr.Phylzzz (Amphetamine Reptile Records) returns to the road. Hot off of their tour with Melvins and Boris, Mr.P is going to summon up the spirits of fellow two-piece trash dogs BEDTIMEMAGIC, the wall-to-wall hedonism of Providence’s Magic Thinking Ape! Fans of stylized band names will be most pleased. ARTIST BIOS: •Mr.Phylzzz Formed in 2015 by founding member Clinton Jacob as a joke. Mr.Phylzzz (pronounced Flyzzz) is an ever changing monster of noise. Over time Mr.Phylzzz has formed a heavy wall of sound filled with hooky riffs and melodic vocals- creating a chaotic storm that’s well worth the painful wall of cranked amps and exploding drums. During the growing years, Phylzzz was doing small tours which landed them getting picked up in 2019 by Amphetamine Reptile Records (AmRep) to be featured in the legendary “Dope Guns ‘N Fucking in the Streets” Vol 14 comp. Later that year they released their debut album “Penitent Curtis” (2019), followed by “Cancel Culture Club” (2022) on AmRep. In 2023 the band released “Fat Chance” on Amrep and completed a full US tour supporting The Melvins and Boris. The band is Chicago based. Mr.Phylzzz is comprised of Clinton Jacobs (guitar/vox) & Danny Sein (drums). •BEDTIMEMAGIC Spicy as a very spicy thing, BEDTIMEMAGIC is a two-dog trash rock band from Boston, MA. They formed in 2013. They have at least three records out. Morgan Berns plays drums, foot organ, and does vocals. Nicholas Pentabona also does vocals, and he plays a bass that Morgan made. It’s really loud. They really think they are dogs. It’s a thing. •Magic Thinking Ape Nobody thinks MTA is smelly. Nobody. If you think that, you’re really mean. I don’t think I would want to be your friend if you think that. title: The Schizophonics
description: The Schizophonics Amps screaming. No exit in sight. The Schizophonics kick the door in and never let it close. This San Diego–based three-piece delivers a live show that’s loud and dangerously fun—an all-gas, no-brakes blast of feedback and groove. It’s full-contact rock ’n’ roll: high voltage, high velocity, and sharpened to a blade. The band features Pat Beers on vocals and guitar, Lety Beers on drums, and Sarah Linton on bass. Together they unleash a fuzz-soaked, funk-fueled attack built on pounding rhythm and feral energy. Every song hits like a charge. Every set feels like the floor might give out. Blink and you miss something. Stand still and you get run over. Forged on the road and fueled by motion, The Schizophonics have torn through stages in fourteen countries, earning a reputation as a must-see live act that turns rooms upside down. Channeling the raw spirit of James Brown, Iggy Pop, Jimi Hendrix, Little Richard, and The Sonics, they strip rock back to its most dangerous elements—and set them loose. — Schizophonics Presented by Get To The Gig & MassConcerts Ages: This show is all ages. title: Michael Kameron
description: Michael Kameron SHOW DESCRIPTION: Michael Kameron celebrates his biggest headline show to date. An alternative pop artist from a small town in Wisconsin, Michael Kameron makes music that turns everyday chaos, vulnerability, and confession into something that feels like a movie soundtrack. Built alongside his best friend in a bedroom studio, his music lives somewhere between crashouts and clarity, late-night honesty and emotional release. Joining him are Dexter Suhn and Rowan Grace, rounding out a night of emotional, story-driven performances and songs that linger long after they end. ARTIST BIOS: Michael Kameron is cinema. An alternative pop artist from a small town in Wisconsin, he never remains still, finding himself in new foreign places, feeding his inspiration of making life feel like a movie and creating the soundtrack to it. Michael Kameron is often described as a bold statement layered with vulnerability and confession. Producing music with his best friend in a bedroom, the music is genre fluid, with cinematic elements, and built around mood and storytelling. He has built a whole universe to play in and explore. It’s complex but simple: Crashouts + confessions + long socks = your favorite alt character. — IG: @the.michaelkameron Dexter Suhn is a 21 year-old alternative r&b singer from the San Francisco Bay Area. While still a teenager, he stumbled into producing after landing a cut on SZA’s SOS Deluxe album, generating buzz as a rising producer, guitarist, and gifted songwriter in the West Coast. Now, Suhn is returning to his artist journey in full steam, with plans to release an extended body of work in the near future. — IG: @dextersuhn Rowan Grace is a South Dakota-born singer-songwriter blending soulful vocals, honest storytelling, and pop driven melodies. description: Jackie Evans With special guests to be announced! title: The Saint Cecilia
description: The Saint Cecilia ARTIST BIO: From the outside, Saint Cecilia is a collection of emotional images, love, art, power, passion, lust and verve. They are a driven and unique band from all over the northern hemisphere. In a time that names like Bowie, Hendrix, Brown and Morrison still generate mystery, they mean very little to the musical charts. Actually at a time that music itself seems to mean little to the those charts…Saint Cecilia arrives on fire and ready to shake up and wake up a somewhat sleepy musical world. Yes, they rock and yes, they play, microphones, guitars, bass, drums and whatever else it takes to make music with heart, sparks, rhythm and soul. title: GKit & Magnificent Danger
description: GKit & Magnificent Danger SHOW DESCRIPTION: Join us for a night of reimagined arrangements of both classic and underrated video game music, brought to you by fusion big band GKit and renowned brass band Magnificent Danger. ARTIST BIOS: GKit is an up-and-coming fusion big band that plays reimagined arrangements of both iconic and niche video game tunes. They take inspiration from jazz, latin, funk, rock and many other styles to breathe new life into game music, joining the movement of bringing video games into the live music world with a progressive and creative touch. title: Julia Minkin
description: Julia Minkin SHOW DESCRIPTION: Chicago-based singer-songwriter Julia Minkin is joined by Boston favorites Bowling Shoes and Cate Yoder for an evening of inventive indie music, compelling storytelling, and rich, genre-bending sounds. From shimmering synth-pop and art-rock experimentation to intimate folk melodies, this lineup offers music that’s as intelligent as it is fun. ARTIST BIOS: Julia Minken: Best known for co-writing viral hit songs with French electropop sensation Kid Francescoli, Chicago-based singer-songwriter Julia Minkin steps into her own with her debut album Not Ready, co-created and produced with her husband Andrew Sudhibhasilp. Blending warm, folk-tinged vocals with nostalgic dance-floor energy and introspection, Minkin “finds her own creative voice, shimmering, rhythmic, and heartfelt—both bold and refreshingly sincere” (Thoughts Words Actions). Bowling Shoes: Melding innovative art-pop experimentalism with indie-rock nuance and arena-ready hooks, Boston, MA’s Bowling Shoes craft eminently catchy music sprinkled with delightful touches of subversive noise Cate Yoder: A double and electric bassist and guitarist from Richmond, Virginia, Cate Yoder learns about her environment through exploring, inventing, and performing a multitude of genres or really any music she can get hands on. Since being established primarily as a bass player, she is diving into the songwriting indie folk role with her band of talented women, performing in the Boston area. With airy melodies, detailed guitar, piano, and percussive elements, and bitter lyrics, she hopes to share her experience of finding solace and comfort in a complex world. title: GHOSTWOMAN
description: GHOSTWOMAN GHOSTWOMAN itself only exists because Uschenko and van Dessel were the ones “stupid enough to commit to it”. Conceived by Uschenko after cutting his teeth as a touring multi-instrumentalist, the project was brought to life in an abandoned farmhouse in Diamond City, Alberta. There, for two months, he would make the self-released, self-titled debut album which was produced and dubbed directly to custom-made cassette tapes. The music has always been beautifully inhospitable, earned only by those curious enough to seek it out. — Dine Alone Records Presented by Get To The Gig & MassConcerts Ages: Show age differs by the day. title: Pepita Lo-Fi Friday
description: Lo-Fi Fridays are here! Just like our Lo-Fi weekends but now during the work week! Stop by the “secret” back taproom of our sweet little cafe space every Friday morning for a quiet sanctuary of productivity and peace. Need a bit of quiet time? The Lamplighter + Pepita team are here to bring you a little slice of calm. From here on out, we will open the back taproom from 8am-2pm on Friday mornings for Lo Fi Fridays. Think of it as a designated calming, quiet zone just for our Pepita patrons. We’ll play chill, ambient music to set the vibe, and folks are encouraged to read, work, study, etc. with minimal talking preferred. Grab a coffee and cozy up in the back taproom at our 284 Broadway location to soak up that tranquil energy or to get a jump start on the week ahead. Your weekend brunch plans have never been more relaxing! P.S. If you’re not feeling quiet time, the front taproom will remain open as usual for normal operations.

title: Brewery Yoga
description: Buy your tickets on Eventbrite! Looking for some healthy weekend plans? Join us for a Sunday morning brewery yoga class at Lamplighter Brewing Co.’s Cambridge Crossing (CX) taproom. We’ll gather in the light-filled upstairs taproom for a gentle flow. Space is limited, and reservations are required. Save your spot through Eventbrite here! All yoga levels are welcome! This class is great for beginners, as well as for experienced yogis. We’ll lead you through a guided flow with a focus on stretching, breathing, and light activity – you might work up a light sweat, but nothing too strenuous. Please plan on bringing your own yoga mat. If you don’t have a mat, a large beach towel works as well. The class takes place in our upstairs taproom at Lamplighter Brewing Co.’s CX location (110 N First St, Cambridge MA). Your ticket includes full access to the yoga class as well as a beer, cold brew coffee, or kombucha. Parking: There is street parking available, or the parking garage is available for $10 with Lamplighter validation. Show your ticket to a bartender before or after class to validate! This event is 21+ and all guests must show a valid government-issued ID. Questions? Get in touch: events@lamplighterbrewing.com.

title: Broadway Trivia
description: Attend one of our most beloved, longest standing brewery traditions: Trivia Tuesday! Every Tuesday swing by our Broadway taproom for our weekly trivia night. It’s free to compete, and winners get beer money. Here’s how it works: show up with your team of 2 – 6 players starting at 7:00 pm, when we’ll open the doors to the back taproom. Head down the hallway to the back, then snag a seat. All seating is first come first serve, so we recommend arriving early – there generally is a line! The game will start at 7:30 pm, and is about two hours long (with plenty of beer breaks, of course). Questions rotate every week, and cover categories ranging from history, politics, sports, movies, pop culture, music, and more. At the end of the game, 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place teams will be awarded Lamplighter gift cards – good for usage in either of our taprooms and at Pepita Coffee Co. In addition to Trivia Tuesday at our Broadway taproom, we also host weekly trivia at our CX taproom. That game takes place on Monday evenings, and is also free to join for teams of 2 – 6. We’d love to see you at either or both! Hungry? Munch on our signature giant soft pretzels or some crunchy nachos, which are available Tuesday evenings only. You’re also always welcome to bring your own food or order in, ask our staff for their favorite local recommendations. See you at trivia night! You must be 21+ attend, all guests will be asked to show valid government ID. Questions? Get in touch! You can reach us at events@lamplighterbrewing.com

title: Brewery Tour & Tasting
description: Break out your notebook and freshly sharpened No. 2 pencils because we’re going back to school! We're offering brewery tours at our original 284 Broadway location on the first Saturday of every month. Space is limited, so snag your spot right here by purchasing a ticket. Our knowledgeable team will lead you on an interactive, behind-the-scenes tour of the production floor at Lamp, where you’ll learn the essentials of craft beer-making, and how it all works at our compact, Cambridge-based facility. You'll also taste your way through the brewing process, sampling three of our current favorite draft pour picks, plus a special bonus beer to start the sipping syllabus. Will you graduate top of your class? Either way, we think you’ll find your new favorite subject. Each ticket includes: 🍻One 6 oz welcome beer, plus 3 - 5 oz flight glass-sized samples 🚶🏼A 60 min guided tasting and behind-the-scenes brewery tour 📝 Beer School "quiz" and informational answer key 📚 A Lamplighter Beer School diploma :) Questions? Get in touch! events@lamplighterbrewing.com. Please note that this event is 21+ and all guests will be asked to show a valid government-issued ID. Refund Policy We understand that plans sometimes change. If you provide us with more than 24 hours' notice prior to the event start time, we will issue a full refund to your original payment method. Within 24 hours of the start time, we will offer a refund in the form of credit to be used for a future ticketed event hosted by Lamplighter, valid for 1 year. Please note that Eventbrite fees, including processing and service fees, are nonrefundable as they are charged by Eventbrite and not under the control of Lamplighter. Please request refunds through Eventbrite, on your order confirmation page.

title: TCS presents: Shane Torres
description: 18+ w/ 2-Item Suggested Minimum.Shane Torres is a standup comedian, writer, podcaster, and actor who resides in Brooklyn. Produced by Bert and LeeAnn Kreischer, Shane’s very first special THE BLUE EYED MEXICAN was released in December 2023. Vulture named it as one of the stand-up specials not-to-be-missed in 2023, raving “The Blue Eyed Mexican, stands out for its beautiful directness and keen sense of good storytelling. It’s a refreshing combination of delicate and obscene.” It is available to stream on YouTube. Shane can be seen on CONAN (twice), THE LATE SHOW WITH STEPHEN COLBERT, NBC’S LAST COMIC STANDING, HALF HOUR SPECIAL WITH COMEDY CENTRAL, and THIS WEEK FROM THE CELLAR on Comedy Central. You might have heard Shane’s “laconic drawling delivery with deliberate pacing” as the NY Times calls it, on popular podcasts such as BERTCAST WITH BERT KREISCHER, BARSTOOL’S KFC RADIO, DR DREW AFTER DARK, THE HONEYDEW WITH RYAN SICKLER, and ARE YOU GARBAGE and a slew of others. title: Exhibition Tour: Celtic Art Across the Ages
description: Go behind the scenes to learn more about the design, production, and installation of the special exhibition Celtic Art Across the Ages, with exhibition designer Robert Checchi. title: Summer Spotlight Tour
description: Spotlight Tours are designed and led by Harvard undergraduates from a range of academic disciplines. Each tour is focused on objects chosen by the student and provides visitors a unique, thematic view into the collections. Tours typically feature three works of art, embrace a conversational format, and last about 45 minutes. This program is supported by the Ho Family Student Guide Fund. The Ho Family Student Guide Program at the Harvard Art Museums prepares students to develop original, research-based tours of the collections. Through their training, Student Guides gain knowledge of the collections and develop skills in critical thinking, visual analysis, public speaking, and leadership. Find out what the Student Guides are up to anytime on Instagram at @harvardarthappens.

title: Harvard Art Museums at Night
description: Join us for an evening of art, fun, food, and more! Gather with friends and mingle inside our spectacular Italian-inspired courtyard, evoking the energy of a bustling town piazza. DJ C-Zone will set the mood with smooth, curated sounds as you chat, snack, sip, and catch up over bites and drinks available for purchase fromNibble Kitchen, which will feature Taiwanese cuisine, and Night Shift Brewing. Drop in on a tour of Celtic Art Across the Ages and listen to fiddler Jenna Moynihan, back by popular demand! Browse the museum shop for some Celtic-themed goodies and stop by the Materials Lab for a special art-making activity. The galleries are yours to explore, with more than 50 spaces filled with world-class art. Don’t forget to check out our current exhibitions, including Celtic Art Across the Ages, which closes August 2. Harvard Art Museums at Night takes place the last Thursday of every month (holidays permitting), from 5 to 9pm. Each night features a new mix of local talent and community partners to make this a festive occasion for all. WBUR is the media partner for Harvard Art Museums at Night. This event is part of ArtsThursdays, a university-wide initiative supported by Harvard University Committee on the Arts (HUCA).

title: Exhibition Tour: Celtic Art Across the Ages
description: Join this tour to learn more about the metalworking and decorative techniques used to make objects on view in the special exhibition Celtic Art Across the Ages. Led by British Museum curator Sophia Adams, the tour will introduce ancient manufacturing techniques and examine how evolving decorative approaches shaped artistic styles during the European Iron Age. Led by: Sophia Adams, Curator of First Millennium European and Roman Conquest Period Collections, British Museum In Celtic Art Across the Ages (March 6–August 2, 2026), discover the many forms of Celtic creativity and their artistic legacies in this sweeping story that spans ancient to modern times.

title: Gray Area: Compassion and Companionship
description: The 14th-century tale of Saint Roch (Rocco) and his canine companion recounts the pair’s selfless compassion and care for those suffering. Join us to explore how today, amid global challenges such as pandemics and social isolation, the story serves as a reminder of the importance of humanitarian values and solidarity. This talk is part of Gray Area, a series that features members of our staff exploring artworks that capture the complexities of humanity, political landscapes, ethics, ideologies, power dynamics, and critical thinking in our times. Through this series, we hope to encourage people to observe and consider their own individual gray areas, and to think about how their unique experiences guide the choices they make. Led by: Jeanne Burke, Academic and Public Programs Coordinator, Division of Academic and Public Programs

title: Art + Science: Materials and Techniques in Frame Conservation
description: This event does not require registration; see further details below. Have you ever wondered what happens in our conservation labs? Join a member of our Straus Center staff for an informal conversation about their work treating objects in our collections. Taking place just outside the Straus Center in the Lightbox Gallery, this presentation will give you the chance to get up close and hands-on with a selection of tools and materials used by conservation staff. In this session, associate frames conservator href="https://harvardartmuseums.org/about/staff/230">Allison Jackson will talk about materials and techniques in frame conservation. The Straus Center for Conservation and Technical Studies is a world leader in fine arts conservation, research, and training. The center’s laboratories are where conservation, conservation science, and curatorial practice intersect, coming together to enrich the understanding of and care for the approximately 250,000 objects in the Harvard Art Museums collections. Space is limited, and this program is available on a first-come, first-served basis; no registration is required. The Harvard Art Museums offer href="https://harvardartmuseums.org/visit/policies/plan-your-visit">free admission every day, Tuesday through Sunday. Please see the href="https://harvardartmuseums.org/visit/policies/general-policies">museum visit page to learn about our general policies for visiting the museums.

There will be two hour-long sessions offered, one at 11am and one at 2pm. Feel free to attend both programs! Also, check out other projects teens have built at the museums in previous years.

title: New on View: Got Milk?
description: The Dutch Republic was one of Europe’s leading dairy producers in the 17th century, owing to its pastures and drained polders. Grazing herds yielded vast quantities of milk, butter, and cheese, which were exported across the continent and consumed at nearly every meal. Join curatorial fellow Susanne Bartels for a talk about the importance of dairy production in 17th-century Dutch society and how it is reflected in the artworks and literature of the time. This gallery talk is part of our New on View series, highlighting recent gallery installations and presenting new insights into recent acquisitions or old favorites. Led by: Susanne Bartels, Stanley H. Durwood Foundation Curatorial Fellow, Division of European and American Art

title: Decompress with Rocky Mountains, “Lander’s Peak”
description: Explore Albert Bierstadt’s Rocky Mountains, “Lander’s Peak” through a guided creative writing exercise that invites you to look closely and respond in your own words. title: Museum Class: Seeing Art with Matisse
description: Explore art history through the perspective of Henri Matisse in this four-week class that takes place in the galleries. With an emphasis on close looking and conversation, Matisse scholar Camran Mani will bring you inside the story of how art history delighted, inspired, and challenged this modern artist, and what he thought about topics from ancient sculpture and Islamic art to Cézanne and beyond. The museum was a space of creative adventure for Matisse—this class aims to make it something similar for you. The class will be held every Thursday from September 10 to October 1.

title: Exhibition Preview Day for Friends, Fellows, and Partners
description: We invite Friends, Fellows, and Partners of the museums to be among the first to explore the fascinating exhibition On Location: Drawing the Outdoors (September 18, 2026–January 17, 2027). Discover how an intimate relationship with nature shaped the artistic vision of 19th-century European artists. On Location: Drawing the Outdoors features approximately 140 sketches, watercolors, and pastels by artists including J. M. W. Turner, Berthe Morisot, Paul Cézanne, and Vincent van Gogh, all inspired by the natural world. Organized as a series of thematic journeys through the landscape, the exhibition explores changing ideas about nature, environmental awareness, and artistic identity. It invites visitors to reflect on why these artists’ experiences of the outdoors continue to resonate today. This special preview is our way of thanking you for your support and dedication to the Harvard Art Museums. To become a Friend, Fellow, or Partner, please visit our Support page. Join today to take advantage of this exclusive opportunity. Funding for On Location: Drawing the Outdoors and related programming was provided by the Stanley H. Durwood Foundation Support Fund, the Stanley H. Durwood Foundation Support Fund for the Study of Dutch Drawing, the Melvin R. Seiden and Janine Luke Fund for Publications and Exhibitions, and the M. Victor Leventritt Lecture Series Endowment Fund. The catalogue was made possible by the Andrew W. Mellon Publication Funds, including the Henry P. McIlhenny Fund. Additional project support was provided by the Almathea Charitable Foundation.

title: Materials Lab Workshop: Landscape Drawing with Optical Devices
description: Join curatorial assistant for special exhibitions and publications Meghan Grady and Harvard physics professor Aravinthan Samuel for a workshop focused on art and science. You’ll first experiment with physical drawing aids, such as perspective frames and camera lucidas, which have helped artists translate complex spaces and details into two dimensions for centuries. Through making, close looking, and a focused gallery visit, participants will explore how such tools work. Grady will share how scientific imaging can inform our understanding of artistic process, accuracy, and style. She researched these techniques for On Location: Drawing the Outdoors, an exhibition featuring 19th-century European drawings and watercolors, and will offer a focused tour explaining how such tools were used in the works on view. Harvard physics professor Aravinthan Samuel will provide an overview of the history of optics in art. During our time together, you’ll create your own gridded frame and take part in a plein air landscape drawing session. You’ll also get the chance to try your hand at applying the devices explored in the workshop. This workshop is one of four offered this fall that explore different media through the lens of art and science. Take one or take them all! title: Materials Lab Workshop: Color Alchemy—Pigments and DIY Paint
description: Join paintings conservator Kate Smith and research curator Francesca Bewer for a workshop focused on art and science. You’ll first experiment with a range of pigments from across the ages. You’ll also make your own paints, then compare how the same pigment behaves across different media and surfaces. Learn about the challenges and rewards of re-creating historical paint recipes and the chemical processes behind “lake pigments” like carmine. Then, looking closely at a selection of artworks in the collections, you’ll discover how scientific imaging helps identify materials the artist used; how aging processes shape the appearance of paintings over time; and how museums respond to these changes. You’ll leave with your own test charts, a set of observations about color’s many transformations, and ideas for at‑home experiments. This workshop is one of four offered this fall that explore different media through the lens of art and science. Take one or take them all! The four workshops are: Saturday, September 19: Landscape Drawing with Optical Devices Wednesday, October 7: Color Alchemy—Pigments and DIY Paint Friday, November 6: Making an Impression Friday, November 20: Casting Connections—Molds, Replicas, and Questions of Authorship

title: Materials Lab Workshop: How to Draw a Pot
description: Hand-drawn, painstakingly measured illustrations of excavated artifacts are key tools in archaeological research. Celebrate International Archaeology Day by joining Cathy Alexander, archaeological illustrator for Harvard’s Archaeological Exploration of Sardis in western Türkiye, and Caitlin Chien Clerkin, archaeologist and research curator for ancient art, to learn how these technical drawings are made and used. Then try your hand at the precise drafting process yourself!

title: Materials Lab Workshop: Making an Impression
description: Join assistant paper conservator Abby Schleicher and research curator Francesca Bewer for a workshop focused on art and science. You’ll discover how different printmaking techniques record both intentional design and the physical traces of making. Through hands-on experimentation using a variety of tools, pressures, inks, and papers, you’ll see how each technical choice leaves distinct traces—and why no two impressions are ever truly identical. We’ll look at a selection of prints under magnification and specialized conservation lighting to “read” their toolmarks, plate wear, inking, and condition. Linking studio experiments with close looking from a conservation perspective, this workshop will give you a concrete framework for identifying print processes and a richer appreciation of the material complexity of printed images. This workshop is one of four offered this fall that explore different media through the lens of art and science. Take one or take them all! The four workshops are: Saturday, September 19: Landscape Drawing with Optical Devices Wednesday, October 7: Color Alchemy—Pigments and DIY Paint Friday, November 6: Making an Impression Friday, November 20: Casting Connections—Molds, Replicas, and Questions of Authorship

title: Pop-Up Renaissance Concert
description: The Harvard Viol Consort, a group of students from Harvard’s course Performance and Culture: Renaissance Music (Music 181R), will put on a pop-up concert in the Calderwood Courtyard. The course is taught by Professor Kate van Orden and assisted by Laura Jeppesen. The performers will play compositions for viol by William Byrd, John Dowland, Diego Ortiz, Anthony Holborne, and other Renaissance composers.

title: Materials Lab Workshop: Casting Connections—Molds, Replicas, and Questions of Authorship
description: Join research curator Francesca Bewer for a workshop focused on art and science. We’ll explore the intimate connections between models, molds, and casts; how molds and casts have been used to produce, replicate, and preserve three-dimensional objects; and what these objects can teach us about skill, technology, and value. Working with clay, plaster, wax, alginate, and silicone putty, we’ll experiment with different processes of molding and casting. Along the way, you’ll be introduced to the scientific tools used to investigate and identify the traces of process and change. Through discussion and comparison with historical plaster casts, wax models, and other surrogates in the Harvard Art Museums collections, we’ll ask when a copy might be considered “fake,” “genuine,” or something in between, and how replicas support research, teaching, and conservation in museums today. This workshop is one of four offered this fall that explore different media through the lens of art and science. Take one or take them all! The four workshops are: Saturday, September 19: Landscape Drawing with Optical Devices Wednesday, October 7: Color Alchemy—Pigments and DIY Paint Friday, November 6: Making an Impression Friday, November 20: Casting Connections—Molds, Replicas, and Questions of Authorship

title: Harvard Art Museums at Night
description: Make your holiday season more festive at the Harvard Art Museums! Join us for an evening of art, fun, food, and more! Gather with friends and mingle inside our spectacular Italian-inspired courtyard, evoking the energy of a bustling town piazza. DJ C-Zone will set the mood with smooth, curated sounds as you chat, snack, sip, and catch up over bites and drinks available for purchase from local vendors. Get a head start on your holiday shopping by taking advantage of a 10% discount at the museum shop. Drop in on a Spotlight Tour, then make art in the Materials Lab. You can also enter to win an original work from the Harvard Ceramics Program! The galleries are yours to explore, with more than 50 spaces filled with world-class art. There are prizes to be won, friends to be made, and favorite artworks to be found! Don’t forget to check out our current exhibitions. Harvard Art Museums at Night takes place the last Thursday of every month (holidays permitting), from 5 to 9pm. Each night features a new mix of local talent and community partners to make this a festive occasion for all. WBUR is the media partner for Harvard Art Museums at Night. This event is part of ArtsThursdays, a university-wide initiative supported by Harvard University Committee on the Arts (HUCA).

title: Second Saturdays Story Time
description: Know Before You Go How to join: Check in at the Visitor Services desk in the Calderwood Courtyard. Fee: This is a free event. Age restrictions: Ages 3 to 7. Caregivers must be present with their children. Accessibility accommodations: Email href="mailto:amregister@harvard.edu">amregister@harvard.edu at least 48 hours in advance, including the name and date of the program in the subject line. General info: The href="https://harvardartmuseums.org/visit/policies/plan-your-visit">museum visit page has general guidelines for your visit. Join us for Second Saturdays Story Time in the galleries, an event in partnership with librarians from Cambridge, Somerville, Watertown, and Medford. In this wonderful, art-filled experience held every second Saturday of the month, librarians will choose thematic books to share with you and yours. This program is organized in partnership with the Cambridge Public Library, Somerville Public Library, Watertown Public Library, and Medford Public Library.

title: Exhibition Tour: On Location: Drawing the Outdoors
description: Discover how artists’ intimate and reflective relationship with nature shapes their artistic vision on an in-depth tour of the special exhibition On Location: Drawing the Outdoors, led by exhibition curator Joachim Homann. On Location features drawings by J. M. W. Turner, John Constable, Gustave Courbet, Edouard Manet, Berthe Morisot, Paul Cézanne, and Vincent van Gogh, among many others. The exhibition is on view from September 18, 2026 to January 17, 2027. Funding for the exhibition and related programming was provided by the Stanley H. Durwood Foundation Support Fund, the Stanley H. Durwood Foundation Support Fund for the Study of Dutch Drawing, the Melvin R. Seiden and Janine Luke Fund for Publications and Exhibitions, and the M. Victor Leventritt Lecture Series Endowment Fund. The catalogue was made possible by the Andrew W. Mellon Publication Funds, including the Henry P. McIlhenny Fund. Additional project support was provided by the Almathea Charitable Foundation.

title: Afmohip: Traveling Village
description: Under the direction of Mrs. JoJo Caidor, Afmohip proudly presents our first-ever full evening-length show, Traveling Village. A work rooted in the past, present, community, and connections.Traveling Village is a sequel that represents communities from different ethnic groups, paving the way and creating connections between the past and the present. It shows the beginnings of shared resources and mutual support, leading to the collective power found in solidarity. The strength of a single, shared force brings unison, togetherness, and courage. It acknowledges that struggles existed before and continue today, while reminding us of the reasons behind our current way of life. At its core, it emphasizes the importance of receiving, understanding, and sharing, allowing communities to endure and grow.

title: Thom Tran
description: Thom Tran Thom Tran is a Los Angeles–based comedian, actor, musician, and U.S. Army combat veteran whose stand-up career began after surviving a gunshot wound to the back of the head while deployed to Iraq. Following his medical retirement, Tran relocated to Los Angeles in 2008 and quickly immersed himself in the comedy scene. He went on to found The GIs of Comedy, an internationally touring, all-military veteran stand-up group that has performed for U.S. service members stationed and deployed in combat zones worldwide. The group was featured on Larry Charles’ Dangerous World of Comedy (Netflix) and has appeared on CBS and NBC. As a solo act, Tran tours nationally and internationally, including dates across Europe with longtime collaborator Brad Williams, performing in Denmark, Norway, England, Ireland, and beyond. His material blends sharp observational humor with lived experience, delivered with discipline and timing honed both on stage and in service. Based in Hollywood, Tran is a regular at premier clubs including the World Famous Laugh Factory and the Comedy & Magic Club, in addition to theaters and venues throughout Southern California. On screen, Tran has co-starred on NCIS: Los Angeles and SEAL Team (CBS) and appears in the feature film My Dead Friend Zoe alongside Morgan Freeman, Sonequa Martin-Green, and Ed Harris. title: Experimental Sketch Workshop with Andy Miara
description: Experimental Sketch Workshop with Andy Miara If you’re a sketch writer, performer, director or teacher who is interested in process, experimentation and discovery, this workshop is for you! This full day session will operate like a professional sketch rehearsal with a focus on material generation and productive exploration. Through writing, improvisation and on-our-feet exercises, we’ll play with a range of techniques to create material. Participants will leave with new creative tools, and new ways to approach writing, performing and developing sketch. Participants should have some prior experience with sketch comedy. A comfort with improvisation is a plus. Come ready to play and let’s see what we can make together! ABOUT ANDY: Andy Miara is a former director for The Second City in Chicago where he also served as a core writing instructor in the Second City Training Center. He is a former head writer of The Onion News Network and co-creator of The Onion’s sister site, Clickhole.com. Alongside Tim Robinson and Mark Raterman, Miara co-founded the sketch group My Mans. The trio developed pilots for Comedy Central and Adult Swim, and created The Thanksgiving House, an immersive theater show in Los Angeles produced by Funny or Die and IFC. Miara has written on animated comedies including Robot Chicken and SuperMansion, and has developed original projects with NBC, TBS, truTV, and Cartoon Network. Most recently, he co-wrote and directed the scripted audio series Get It To Dutch for iHeart Media, and currently has an animated pilot in development at Fox starring Tim Robinson and Cecily Strong. Miara is an Assistant Professor of Screenwriting at Emerson College. Doors: 9:30 AM Start: 10:00 AM End: 4:00 PM Age Limit: This workshop is 18+ Refund Policy: All sales are final. No Refunds. title: Sunset Boulevard by Moonstruck Theater Company
description: Sunset Boulevard Show Description: Winner of ten Tony Awards including Best Musical, Andrew Lloyd Webber’s Sunset Boulevard is a dark, glittering descent into Hollywood obsession. title: Wrestling with the Written Word: A Clown & Physical Theatre Workshop with Sheriden Thomas
description: Wrestling with the Written Word: A Clown & Physical Theatre Workshop with Sheriden Thomas SHOW DESCRIPTION: It is, and is not the words. It’s the situation. You, your partner(s), and imagination in the moment are the situation…. We will be fooling around with written words, using the Dynamics, the Complicities, the Clown Personas, and the Tension States, as a fruitful path for mining the physical and the fun. Very brief texts of Will Shakespeare & Sam Beckett will be supplied…. And you can bring your own. A monologue, a scene, a poem, a manifesto. It’s all grist, darlin’. ARTIST BIO: Over several decades, Sheriden has acted under Actor’s Equity Contracts in the nation’s regional theatres. Starting in the 70’s, playing ingénues for the Guthrie Theatre in Minneapolis to Boston’s Moonbox Productions, garnering a Boston Critics Award for Kimberly in Kimberly Akimbo. Recently, in film, she played two old ladies. One in Tiffany Paulson’s About Fate and another in Eric Aronson’s Any Day Now about the Gardner Museum heist. It’s now streaming on Amazon Prime. Sheriden has directed and taught acting at Cornell and Southern Methodist Universities. Since arriving in Boston, she directed plays and readings for Another Country, Queer Soup Productions, and Boston Playwrights’ Theatre. As Senior Lecturer Emerita, at Tufts University, she taught a variety of acting courses including Advanced Acting Lab, Shakespeare, Mask, Physical Comedy, and Acting as Career. She directed a dozen plays, concluding with an edited video of Jeffrey Hatcher’s delightfully, silly adaptation of The Government Inspector. Sheriden has directed professionally for the Shakespeare Festival of Dallas, Mother Jones in Chicago, Company Theatre in Los Angeles, Manhattan Class, and WOW Cafe in New York City. She will be directing The Beauty Queen of Leenane for Theater Uncorked this November at Boston Center for the Arts. Her Tufts bio is: https://tdps.tufts.edu/people/faculty/sheriden-thomas Doors: 10:45 AM Start

title: The Future of Higher Ed (FOHE) Boston Presents: David’s Farewell Spectacular & Search for Boston’s Next Co-Lead
description: The Future of Higher Ed (FOHE) Boston Presents: David’s Farewell Spectacular & Search for Boston’s Next Co-Lead EVENT DESCRIPTION: After helping build FOHE Boston into one of the most vibrant higher education and EdTech communities in the country, David is stepping down as Co-Lead. Join us for an evening of celebration, storytelling, questionable decision-making, and the search for his successor. title: Bubble Burlesque: Denim Diaspora
description: Bubble Burlesque: Denim Diaspora Step into a world where rebellion meets rhinestones, and fabric tells a story far deeper than fashion. Denim & Desire is a burlesque experience that peels back the seams of history, celebrating denim not just as an icon of style, but as a symbol woven through Black resilience, labor, culture, and expression. From its roots as durable workwear worn by enslaved and working class Black laborers, to its transformation into a global statement of cool shaped by Black musicians, dancers, and tastemakers, denim has always carried more than meets the eye. August 16th, we honor that legacy, thread by thread, strip by strip. Expect a dazzling lineup of performers who will reimagine denim in all its forms, raw, rugged, glamorous, and subversive. Through tease, storytelling, and unapologetic sensuality, each act pays tribute to the Black bodies and voices that turned denim into a canvas of identity and power. This is more than a show. It is a reclamation. A celebration. A strut through history in your best blues. So grab your seats, hold onto your hems, and get ready to witness denim like you have never seen it before. Denim is in our genes. From our enslaved ancestors dressed in negro cloth, to the denim clad cowboys on dude ranches, to denim being reclaimed and made into a statement of rebellion in the civil rights movement, to the repositioning of denim in the world of fashion due in part to black taste makers. On August 16th at The Rockwell, join Bubble Burlesque and an Iconic all black cast to find out how we continue to set your tongue. title: Frank Sriracha: Home is Where the Stage is
description: Frank Sriracha: Home is Where the Stage is Frank Sriracha is one of the most celebrated cabaret legends the world has ever seen. Tonight, he finally gets what he deserves: a Lifetime Achievement Award. Frank Sriracha has spent decades performing for crowds of adoring fans all over the European Black Box Circuit. But tonight, the Wonderkid of the Sunset Strip returns for his big award. First, Frank will give his big acceptance speech, and maybe sing a song. Then after like 5 or 10 minutes, everyone will get up and head to the massive gala reception with a fully catered Branzino dinner, open bar, and hundreds of dollars worth of free swag . So it’s only a five or ten minute speech in the theater, and then everyone will leave. But no one can leave until Frank gives his big speech, so it might be more like thirteen or eighteen minutes but there’s a huge free dinner after. Could be 20. Nominated for Best World Premiere & Take the Stage Award at the Hollywood Fringe Festival. “Max Charbonneau has an infectious charisma” – LA Weekly – LA Hidden Gems. “I think I just saw the funniest show in all of Fringe” – Stage Takes —– ARTIST SOCIAL MEDIA: @corndudemax @franksrirachareal ARTIST BIOS: Max Charbonneau (he/him) is a clown, writer, and performer based in beautiful Los Angeles. title: Clown Intensive w Gemma Soldati
description: Clown Intensive w Gemma Soldati DESCRIPTION: Discover and reunite with your playful spirit and comedic vocabulary in this workshop of fun. Using clown, physical games, costume and improvisation, we’ll explore our imagination, pleasure, and our relationship with an audience. This workshop will help participants unleash their muse and confront their doubt. We’ll find what we may have lost or forgotten on our journey to become “good.” This class is for folks of all experience levels who are ready to take their comedic practice to the next level in a supportive and creative environment. IG: @Sleepyheadshow BIO: “Gemma’s absolute fearlessness matches her commitment to the absurd” – Comedy Bureau Gemma Soldati is an American performing and teaching artist. She won Best Comedy at the 2019 Melbourne Fringe with The Living Room. She has taught in Los Angeles, NYC, New England, Chicago, and Toronto for both adults and children. She was a 2023/24 resident at Ars Nova’s Makers Lab in NYC. Gemma’s focus is clown inspired work developed in front of live audiences. Her projects playfully dive deep into the heart of vital themes probing audiences with questions and meaning making – Grief, Ritual, Sleep, Dreams, Money, Power and beyond. Her current project is The Adventures of Sleepyhead, an all ages show, book and in-development tv program about a dreamer named Sleepyhead. DATES : September 19 & 20, 2026 DOORS : 9:30 AM START : 10:00 AM END : 3:00 PM AGES : 18+ TICKET PRICE : $200/250/300 CAPACITY : 16 The Rockwell is ADA Accessible. No refunds within 7 days of the workshop.

title: Jonathan Vale: Underground Magic
description: Some magicians pull rabbits from hats. Jonathan Vale pulls thoughts from your head. Enter the underground world of Jonathan Vale: where mind-reading, psychological illusions, and storytelling collide in a hypnotic journey that’s both intimate and dangerously convincing. Armed with little more than a deck of cards, a sharp wit, and a spellbinding gaze, Jonathan turns perception, fear, and dreams into an evening you can’t quite explain afterward. This isn’t a “tricky” show. Underground Magic is a mesmerizing descent into what’s real. You’ll witness impossible predictions, eerie coincidences, and deeply human storytelling, delivered with the friendly-yet-mysterious flair that’s made Jonathan a favorite across New England. You’ll laugh. You’ll gasp. You’ll leave wondering: How the **** did he do that? Come skeptical. Leave amazed. Artist Bio: Jonathan Vale is a magician, mentalist, and keynote speaker who blends mental-magic and life’s deep questions into performances that feel like glimpses into the mind. Creator of the one-man theater productions Magic Late at Night and Underground Magic, he’s taken the stage at TEDx, Fenway Park, Boston College, and for universities and corporate audiences across New England. In 2026, he appeared as a resident magician at The Hand and Eye in Chicago — one of the magic world’s most prestigious venues– for a multiple-show run to sold-out crowds. title: “Be Good” with Paulette
description: “Be Good” with Paulette OH LOOK! HERE COMES THE MILDEST MAN IMAGINABLE. Paulette stumbles into a room full of the most strangers he’s ever seen, and he doesn’t know whether to panic or mingle—so he does both, for 60 minutes. Sporting a brown sweater and a hot-off-the-fist black eye, he dares to address the room armed with nothing but an arsenal of pleasantries and a monumental fear of rejection. Hot off of a high octane tour of Europe, the UK, and even the east coast of America, certified clown Daniel Maseda brings well-mannered idiot Paulette back to The Rockwell for the very second time with this fan-favorite show that never plays out the same way twice. A perfect evening for anyone who wants to scream at a polite person. Fringie Award (Clown), Philly Fringe 2025 Pick of the Fringe, Edinburgh Fringe 2025 (Mervyn Stutter) Best of the Fringe, District Fringe 2025 (DC Theater Arts) ★★★★½ “Utterly ridiculous…brilliantly performed…laugh-out-loud delirium.” (DC Theater Arts) ★★★★ “For this hour, just say yes to the madness.” (The Comic’s Comic) ARTIST SOCIAL MEDIA: IG @da.nee.ell ARTIST BIOS: Daniel Maseda (he/him) is a performer from Washington, DC who makes ridiculous work. He is currently touring his solo performance “BE GOOD!” WITH PAULETTE, which played at the 2025 Edinburgh Fringe (★★★★, Pick of the Fringe) and was awarded the inaugural Fringie for best Clown performance at the 2025 Philadelphia Fringe. Alongside his performance work, Daniel teaches workshops on clown, improvisation, and devising. He is a graduate of École Philippe Gaulier. description: Jaboukie Young – White ARTIST BIO: Jaboukie Young-White is a comedian, writer, filmmaker, and musician from Chicago who was a correspondent on THE DAILY SHOW WITH TREVOR NOAH. Jaboukie also voices the lead roles of “Truman” in the animated series FAIRFAX on Amazon, and the role of “Ethan” in Disney’s STRANGE WORLD. Most recently, Jaboukie can be seen in THE THREESOME, directed by Chad Hartigan, which just premiered at SXSW 2025 and the Warner Brothers feature film, COMPANION, directed by Drew Hancock, now streaming. title: Tame Your Inner Critic: A Live Book Launch & Interactive Workshop with Caitlin Green
description: Tame Your Inner Critic: A Live Book Launch & Interactive Workshop with Caitlin Green What becomes possible when you stop believing your inner critic? Join author and self-trust coach Caitlin Green for an inspiring and interactive evening celebrating the launch of her debut book, Tame Your Inner Critic . More than a traditional book launch, this experience blends storytelling, practical psychology, mindfulness, and guided reflection to help you build a more compassionate relationship with yourself. Whether your inner critic shows up as perfectionism, self-doubt, people-pleasing, or the feeling that you’re never quite enough, you’ll leave with practical tools you can begin using immediately to cultivate greater confidence, resilience, and lasting self-trust. The evening includes: ● A live author talk ● Interactive workshop exercises ● Audience Q&A ● Book signing ● Time to connect with others in a welcoming community Whether you’re navigating a career transition, healing from burnout, working toward a personal goal, or simply longing to be kinder to yourself, this evening is an invitation to stop fighting yourself—and start trusting yourself. Come for the book. Leave with a new relationship with yourself. Date: Sunday, November 15, 2026 Location: The Rockwell, Somerville, MA Doors: 4:00 PM Presentation & Workshop: 4:30 PM Book Signing & Community Mingling: Following the presentation About Caitlin Green Caitlin Green is a self-trust coach, yoga teacher, and former special educator who helps people transform self-doubt into self-trust through evidence-based psychology, mindfulness, and compassionate self-inquiry. Her work integrates science, storytelling, spirituality, and practical tools that empower people to quiet their inner critic and create lasting change. title: The Jorge Perez-Albela Trio with Kenny Werner & John Lockwood
description: $35 admission / 8pm doors / 8:15 start / seated & standing Peruvian born drummer, percussionist and composer, Jorge Perez-Albela is presenting an unforgettable evening of music improvisation with world class jazz masters, pianist Kenny Werner and bassist John Lockwood. Kenny has been a world-class pianist and composer for over forty years. His prolific output of compositions, recordings and publications continue to impact audiences around the world. In 1996 he wrote his landmark book, Effortless Mastery, Liberating The Master Musician Within. Werner has since created videos, lectured world-wide and authored many articles on how musicians, artists or even business people can allow their “master creator” within to lift their performance to it’s highest level, showing us how to be spontaneous, fearless, joyful and disciplined in our work and in our life. Kenny was awarded the 2010 Guggenheim Fellowship Award for his seminal work, No Beginning No End. No Beginning No End is a musical journey exploring tragedy and loss, death and transition, and the path from one lifetime to the next. Utilizing over 70 musicians, Kenny’s third album for Half Note Records is an expansive composition featuring Joe Lovano, Judy Silvano, Wind Ensemble, Choir and String Quartet. Born in Brooklyn, NY on November 19, 1951 and then growing up in Oceanside, Long Island, Kenny began playing and performing at a young age, first recording on television at the age of 11. Although he studied classical piano as a child, he enjoyed playing anything he heard on the radio. In high school and his first years of college he attended the Manhattan School of Music as a classical piano major. His natural instinct for improvisation led Kenny to the Berklee School of Music in 1970. There he sought tutelage of the renowned piano teacher Madame Chaloff. A Her gracious wisdom and inspiration became a driving force in Kenny’s conception: A music conscious of its spiritual intent and essence. From Boston, Kenny travel

title: Elan Mehler Trio
description: Elan Mehler has released 11 albums as a leader, with such musicians as Bill Frisell, Dave Douglas, Becca Stevens, Scott Robinson, Francisco Mela and many more and has garnered stellar reviews from such publications as The New York Times, The Guardian, Jazz Times, and Downbeat. His latest record is a solo piano record released on Sunnyside Records that has garnered significant press. Elan has brought his projects to clubs and festivals worldwide including Birdland, Queen Elizabeth Hall, and the North Sea Festival. In 2016 Elan co-founded the label Newvelle Records, as artistic director of the label he has signed and produced over 50 records by artists such as Jack DeJohnette, John Patitucci, Dave Liebman, Lionel Loueke, Irma Thomas and Ellis Marsalis. Reviews and music available at www.elanmehler.com Max Ridley is one of the most in-demand bassists in the Boston area. He was awarded full-tuition scholarships to study at Berklee College of Music for both undergraduate and graduate degrees, earning his graduate degree from the extremely exclusive Berklee Global Jazz Institute under the direction of master pianist, educator and humanitarian Danilo Perez. An equally important part of his education was down the street from Berklee at Boston’s historic Wally’s Jazz Cafe. He began going to jam sessions there in high school and eventually became the house bass player every Friday and Saturday night.Ridley has played and recorded with renowned musicians of many different styles all over the world. An incredibly versatile multi-instrumentalist, Max performs regularly in bands playing Jazz, Rock, Folk, Soul, Punk, Klezmer, Polka and every other style you can think of. He also serves as the music director for tap dance company Subject:Matter (https://www.subjectmattertap.com/) and teaches music as a guest lecturer at different colleges around New England (such as Longy School of Music, University of New Hampshire and Berklee College of Music). title: Jerry Bergonzi Quartet
description: Jerry Bergonzi, Tenor Saxophone A fine, high-powered tenor saxophonist with a tone influenced by John Coltrane, a mastery of chord changes, and a strong musical imagination, Jerry Bergonzi has long had an underground following in the Boston area. He started on clarinet when he was eight, switching to alto at 12, and finally to tenor two years later. Bergonzi was inspired early on by Sonny Rollins, Coltrane, and Hank Mobley. He attended Lowell University and then after graduation played electric bass in local bands behind singers and strippers, saving up enough money to move to New York in 1972. After struggling in the Big Apple for seven years and gaining some recognition as a member of Two Generations of Brubeck and of the Dave Brubeck Quartet (with whom he appeared on several Concord albums during 1979-1981), Bergonzi moved back to Boston in 1981, where he developed a strong career both as a tenorman and as an educator. He has since led several groups (including two called Con Brio and Gonz) and recorded for the Plug, Not Fat, Red, and Blue Note labels. — By Scott Yanow, AllMusic

title: The Fringe
description: The Fringe originally formed back in 1971 by tenor-saxophonist George Garzone, bassist Richard Appleman, and drummer Bob Gullotti as an outlet for their free jazz improvisations, The Fringe have entertained and enlightened Boston area jazz audiences for over 50 years. Bassist Appleman left the band in 1985 to become Chairman of the Bass Department at Berklee College and was replaced by veteran bassist John Lockwood. Bob Gullotti passed away in 2020 and is remembered as one of the greatest jazz drummers of his generation. Francisco Mela, now on drums, graciously fills the space Bob left behind. Along with their impressive tenure with The Fringe, Garzone, Lockwood, and Mela are in great demand as session players and have played with many of the greats of contemporary jazz. Along with keeping up with a busy performance schedule, each of them are well-respected educators helping to inspire the jazz musicians of tomorrow. title: Todd Marcus - Virginia MacDonald Quintet
description: $30 advance / $35 at the door / $15 students / 7:30pm doors / seated & standing Todd Marcus - Virginia MacDonald Quintet Since 2022, Baltimore bass clarinetist Todd Marcus and Toronto clarinetist Virginia MacDonald have been performing and touring together across the United States and Canada with their quintet. Their work together presents a lush ensemble that showcases the range of beauty and power by the clarinet in a modern jazz context, with repertoire comprised of original compositions by both bandleaders. They have performed at jazz festivals and prominent venues internationally including Smalls Jazz Club, the Toronto Jazz Festival, the International Clarinet Association, and the Baltimore Museum of Art. Playing the clarinet is challenging (due technical and volume complexities) which leads most woodwind musicians to use saxophones and avoid using clarinets in more intense modern jazz. While the clarinet has a rich history in traditional New Orleans and Dixieland music, swing era big band contexts, and avant-garde free playing, it is significantly underutilized in modern straight-ahead jazz. Marcus and MacDonald have filled this gap for the clarinet in modern jazz. Their unique solo and compositional voices have established a prominence and international reputation on their instruments in jazz today. Their musical partnership showcases the versatility of the clarinet and captures audiences with a new and unique musical experience. Warrenbuwa will be accompanied by Shri Rajesh Pai on tabla and Shri Yash Barhate on harmonium. “.an amazing man, an amazing artist.”— Ustad Amjad Ali Khan, interviewed in Little India, September 2002 — ”Warren’s talent of keeping listeners engrossed by his delightful singing.comes fromthis same attitude of heartily enjoying the process of musical discovery.”— Chaitanya Kunte, Tarun Bharat, Pune, India —LIVE-STREAMING WILL BE AVAILABLE: please contact Gabe Boyarin for more info. 2502178607, gwboyarin@gmail.comcurated by Gabe Boyarin, presented in collaboration with Shadaj

title: Far From Home
description: $15 at the door / $10 advanced tickets / 9pm doors / 9:30 start / standing A collection of indie/folk/alternative singer songwriters sharing original music crafted outside of Boston. With a common passion for music, these four unique artists, Halfwayfrombackwards, We Are The Dirt, Cate Yoder, and Jace, embark on a journey with their show, "Far From Home." Halfwayfrombackwards is a primarily solo (occasionally collaborative) project created by Fredericksburg’s Dylan Cave. Influenced by alternative folk genres, he mixes his southern roots with his emo inclinations to create an experience meant to entertain and make you feel something. Kassi is the lead singer of the band “Wearethedirt”. She writes emotional, heartfelt songs with a somewhat folk-punk & singer-songwriter feel and has music out on all streaming platforms. Performing solo, she will bring an intimate experience that just might make you cry. A double/electric bassist and guitarist from Richmond, Virginia, Cate Yoder learns about her environment through exploring, inventing, and performing a multitude of genres. After being established primarily as a bass player, she is currently diving into the songwriting indie folk scene with her band of talented women, performing in the Boston area. With airy melodies, detailed guitar, piano, and percussive elements, and bittersweet lyrics, she hopes share her experience of finding solace and comfort in a complex world. jace is a singer-songwriter from Manila, Philippines whose music seeks to emulate the feeling of flipping through old photo albums.

title: Awaken 2026 Live Breathwork
description: Breathwork is one of the fastest-growing self-healing modalities in the United States. Breathwork refers to a variety of types of breathing exercises or techniques that involve intentionally changing your breathing patterns that are done to improve mental, physical, and spiritual well-being. During a live experience an expert Breathwork Facilitator will guide you through using your own breath to heal yourself from the inside out. The work combines cognitive catharsis, powerful somatic release, and re-connection to your heart which often results in the intense emotional and physical release of stuck energy, repressed emotions, blockages, and unprocessed traumas.​ Many attendees claim that what they experienced during is far superior to any kind of therapy, healing retreats, and transformational seminars they have tried before. It is a full spectrum of emotions. After the event you will come back to your true-self and feel empowered to transform your life in 2026 through just a SINGLE NIGHT of deep work.

title: Bill Blumenreich Presents: Chill Towards Enlightenment: A Stoke Seminar with Chad Goes Deep
description: A satirical ted talk seminar on his stoke philosophy where he tackles the question: “Why is bummer so prevalent in our society and how do we transcend it?” Join us on this beautiful journey and learn Chad’s transformative technique, The Chill Method, which will help you reclaim your inner joy and set you on a new path to enjoy this radical adventure we call life.

title: Somerville Fermentation Festival
description: A celebration of food and culture in Somerville, MA Join us for the second year of the Somerville Fermentation Festival, an annual celebration of the world of fermented foods and the layers of community that create them! Sample & take home a diverse range of fermented foods & beverages, learn how to make your own sauerkraut, swap starter cultures with other local fermenters, and attend presentations by experts in the field.

title: A Cell Phone Movie - screening
description: Struggling, out of work actor Will Sterling made a feature film entirely on his cell phone about a fictional version of himself, a similarly struggling, out of work actor making a movie on his cell phone about a struggling, out of work actor making a movie on his cell phone. The result is “A Cell Phone Movie,” a $20k micro-budget meta-comedy that’s just as chaotic as it is self aware. Nominated for best debut at Raindance, it blurs the lines between reality and fiction as it explores artistic obsession, failing on purpose, and refusing to give up on a dream. The screening includes a live introduction by Sterling and a post film talk that’s part stand-up comedy, part motivational shove to inspire you to get out there and make the d*mn thing!

title: Poly Poly Oxen Free
description: Each show features The Catch who already has at least one love and is looking for more. The Poly Pool of eligible contestants must complete a series of challenges to woo The Catch. Will love be found in the Poly Pool? Will The Catch make a match or two? Will we all just hook up after the show anyway? This special Boston show will include a partnership with Poly Speed Dating, a Boston-based organization that creates opportunities for ethical non-monogamous people to connect. Upon arriving at the theater, audience members will be invited to complete a brief online compatibility survey. Using Poly Speed Dating’s special platform, participating audience members will be paired with someone in attendance for a speed date during intermission, giving everyone the opportunity to find love. title: Belmont World Film's 23rd Family Festival: Day 4
description: Parents with children ages 3–12 won’t want to miss Belmont World Film’s 23rd Family Festival. Guided by this year’s theme Lights, Camera, Magic!, the festival showcases a diverse selection of films from around the world—many making their North American or U.S. premieres—offering young audiences an immersive and culturally rich cinematic experience. It’s a wonderful way to “travel the world” during MLK Weekend and beyond without the cost or hassle of a trip. The festival takes place at the West Newton Cinema from January 17–18, the Brattle Theatre on Monday, January 19, the Belmont Media Center on Saturday, January 24, and the Regent Theatre on Sunday, January 25. This year’s lineup includes mostly North American premieres, with more than half of the films adapted from or inspired by classic and contemporary children’s books—a longstanding festival hallmark. For young readers and those who struggle with reading, a professional voice-over will read subtitles aloud for films in languages other than English, creating an experience much like story time. Your children can also engage in hands-on workshops--including Learn to the Draw the Minions and Hotel Transylvania Characters and Introduction to Storyboarding for Animated Films--with this year’s Artists-in-Residence, story artist and director Dave Feiss and story artist and writer Paul McEvoy, both of whom have most recently worked on The SpongeBob Movie: Search for SquarePants, as well as the Minions and Hotel Transylvania franchises and many others. Purchase tickets in advance only at https://www.belmontworldfilm.org/family-festival or in person on day of show at the box office (cash only).
cost: Shorts programs: $8. Feature length films: $12. Workshops: $22. Films Only Pass: $40. VIP Full Access Pass: $100. Save $8 on 4-packs.

title: 6 Week Art Makers Series @The Foundry
description: Paint Your Truth: 6-Week Community Solidarity Series Join us in person for a fun and inspiring 6-week journey of creativity and connection! "Paint Your Truth" is all about coming together to express your unique story through art while building community solidarity. Whether you're a beginner or a pro, this series is a chill space to share, learn, and grow with others. Don't miss out on this chance to paint, laugh, and connect! Jan 10, 2026 Week 1: Kick off the Winter 2026 series with a grounding and spacious solo-led experience facilitated by Vie Ciné. This session focuses on reconnecting with your inner voice through process painting. Participants are invited to explore color, gesture, and emotion without judgment—giving themselves permission to express freely. We open with a welcoming circle, move through embodied warmups, and journey into two hours of supported painting time. This session sets the tone for the entire series: community, courage, vulnerability, and creative truth-telling. Jan 17, 2026 Week 2: Time: Rhythm & Creative Rituals Guest facilitator Missy Arellano, also known as The Clock Lady, joins Vie for a unique, time-centered creative exploration. Missy works with concepts of rhythm, duration, and personal cycles. Together, Vie and Missy guide participants through reflective prompts, meditative timed exercises, and creative rituals linked to personal and collective rhythms. Participants explore how time shapes their healing and how painting can become a grounding ritual that honors both slowness and momentum. Jan 24 2026 Week 3: Deepening Your Inner Narrative This solo-led session returns to the heart of Paint Your Truth: connecting to your story. Participants move deeper into their creative process with expanded prompts that explore memory, identity, and emotional layering. title: The 16th Annual Martin Luther King Day of Service & Learning
description: Come lend your helping hands and honor Rev.Martin Luther King Jr. by showing up to answer his question: ‘What are you doing for others?” Come for the afternoon or just a short time and join with Cambridge neighbors as we work together to help others. As part of the MLK Day of Service & Learning, we hope you will take part in our many hands-on projects with your Cambridge neighbors…

title: MLK Day Math Festival
description: On 1/17/2026 from 10AM-1PM, the Cambridge Math Circle will be hosting our 8th annual MLK Day Math Festival. Students in grades K-8 and their families are welcome to join us for math games, puzzles, and prizes, celebrating the exciting ways that math can be found all around us. Families can learn more at the link below, and reach out to info@cambridgemathcircle.org with any questions. Register here: cambridgemathcircle.org/mlk-day-festival

title: Rep. Rogers Office Hours January 2026
description: I encourage any and all to stop by and speak with me or my staff about any concerns or to offer any input you might have. Occasionally, my aide will attend office hours in my place and then relay any issues to me. If you wish to speak to me directly, please email me at Dave.Rogers@mahouse.gov so that I can ensure that I will be attending. If I cannot make it, we can always set up a meeting at a mutually convenient time.
